## 1. Prediction market

June 3 was a correction day on [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/brazil-presidential-election) following the sharp repricing of June 2. Flávio Bolsonaro fell back to 32.10% (USD 6.27M), ↓1.3pp in 24h, returning roughly one-third of the +4.2pp jump from the previous day. Lula remained stable at 39.50% (USD 6.09M), and the gap between the two widened back to +7.4pp, from +6.1pp at the previous close. The movement has two components: technical digestion of yesterday's peak and a shift in framing of the U.S. tariff increase (detailed in Section 3), without a single acute trigger on June 3 itself.

The third way remained at floor level, a consequence of the realignment on June 2 in which [Tarcísio closed support for Flávio](https://www.estadao.com.br/politica/flavio-se-reencontra-com-zema-em-minas-gerais-faz-brinde-e-prega-uniao-da-direita/). Renan Santos stabilized at 15.80% (USD 6.55M), holding second place in the presidential market, above Haddad 4.90% (USD 5.38M), Zema 2.40% (USD 3.41M), and Caiado 1.90% (USD 3.80M). In the sub-market for second place in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), Renan appears at 18.70% (USD 1.01M).

In institutional markets, the contract for impeachment of a [STF](/en/glossary#stf) minister before 2027 remained stable at 5.50%, with low volume (USD 80k) that recommends cautious reading. In the [Senate market](https://polymarket.com/event/next-brazil-senate-election-most-seats-won), [PL](/en/glossary#pl) fell to 74.00%, with UNIÃO at 14% (thin book). In the [2026 inflation contract](https://polymarket.com/event/brazil-annual-inflation-2026), the market concentrates probability in the 5.00% to 5.49% band (26%), with the tail at or above 6% still priced around 22.7%.

## 2. What the polling institutes registered

No new national-scope survey on June 3. The national benchmark remains [Real Time Big Data from June 1](https://www.poder360.com.br/) (n=2,000), which measured [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) Lula 38% × Flávio 31% (gap +7pp) and, in the runoff, Lula 45% × 40% over Flávio, with Caiado tying Lula at 43% × 43% and government approval at 42% against 52% disapproval. The [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) flow for the day was entirely state-level, dominated by Veritá institute and presence of Real Time Big Data, [Paraná Pesquisas](/en/glossary#parana-pesquisas), and Vox Brasil in local breakdowns.

It is worth noting that the market gap (+7.4pp) widened again compared to the survey (+7pp in RTBD), undoing the rare convergence observed on June 2, when the market came to price the contest tighter than the institute.

## 3. What the press covered

The agenda of June 3 was dominated by a shift in framing regarding the 25% U.S. tariff increase. What appeared on June 2 as Flávio's leading role became treated as the opposition's political cost: the columnist at [g1](https://g1.globo.com/politica/blog/andreia-sadi/post/2026/06/03/analise-conta-tarifaco-20-mesa-bolsonarismo.ghtml) described the "bill of tariff hike 2.0 on Bolsonarism's tab," and the Planalto, according to [Brasil 247](https://news.google.?oc=5), assesses that the offensive became an "electoral gift" for Lula.

On the diplomatic front, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira that [he wants to continue dialogue on tariffs](https://g1.globo.com/politica/blog/camila-bomfim/post/2026/06/03/secretario-dos-eua-jamieson-greer-diz-a-mauro-vieira-que-quer-continuar-a-dialogar-sobre-tarifas.ghtml), opening a negotiation pathway. On the same front, Vice-President Alckmin stated that ["whenever dialogue advances, false patriot saboteurs undermine negotiations"](https://oglobo.globo.com/blogs/miriam-leitao/post/2026/06/alckmin-sempre-que-o-dialogo-avanca-falsos-patriotas-sabotadores-prejudicam-as-negociacoes.ghtml). On the commercial side, g1 reported that [exports to the U.S. fell 14% in May](https://g1.globo.com/economia/noticia/2026/06/03/exportacoes-para-os-eua-recuam-14percent-em-maio-mas-balanca-comercial-tem-saldo-positivo-de-us-78-bilhoes.ghtml), although the trade balance remains positive.

From the opposition side, Flávio sustained the thesis that the tariff "is Lula's" and that [he will negotiate "on equal footing" with the U.S. if elected](https://news.google.?oc=5), in addition to [defending right-wing unity and predicting PT attacks on Caiado and Zema](https://news.google.?oc=5). Meanwhile, the government, through Lula's voice, maintained offensive rhetoric: the president described State Secretary Marco Rubio as ["anti-Latin America"](https://g1.globo.com/mundo/noticia/2026/06/02/rubio-que-e-anti-america-latina-e-nao-gosta-do-brasil-diz-lula-sobre-secretario-de-trump.ghtml) (statement from June 2) and accused Flávio of being a ["traitor" who hampers negotiations with Trump](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxPLTdMSGstb3dSaWhNQ25RaEZtQXlqUzFZMzBYaExZRVNDeW4ycHZ1WXV3VmZKZGJyMGtnY2dsMHBRSHZ0Y0dQNk40VmY5aTVveTA0RHlzYm1FRFBQalZEZzRIZTJ3OVZQWXFIc2N6cFMtV0tKT1k0ZmRxOGZkOVB6VHhoNmR6Q2ZIaVJCSVZacFRXb2EzU21zWXFmWERGZHV4WWV1dk5SSmlTQQ?oc=5).

On the previous day's agenda that reverberated into the day, Flávio received the title of honorary citizen in Belo Horizonte and [met with Eduardo Cunha](https://news.google.?oc=5), and sealed a reunion with Zema in Minas. On the regional side, [Acre-born Jorge Viana and Gladson Cameli lead the Senate scenario](https://news.google.?oc=5) in state polling.

## 4. Divergences of the day

> **Market × research (Renan):** The market keeps Renan Santos at 15.80%, second place in the presidential race, while Real Time Big Data from June 1 assigns him 6% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). The gap of around 10pp remains the widest on the Dashboard between real money and declared intention.

> **Research × market (Caiado):** The same RTBD shows Caiado [technically tied](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) with Lula at 43% × 43% in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), a sign of competitiveness that the market does not price in: the Caiado contract is worth less than 2%. Here research sees more than real money does—a rare inversion.

> **Market × narrative (tariff increase):** Flávio's retreat in 24h coincides with the shift in framing of the tariff increase from protagonist to passive, but the market movement is also consistent with technical digestion of the June 2 surge. AFOS does not attribute a single cause: it registers the coincidence without asserting that the reframing alone brought down the price.

## In summary

1. [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) corrected part of the previous day's reversal: Flávio returned about a third of the surge, retreated to 32.10%, and the gap to Lula returned to +7.4pp.
2. Without new national research, the reference remains RTBD from June 1 (gap +7pp); the market gap returned to being wider than the research gap, undoing the June 2 convergence.
3. The U.S. tariff increase migrated from protagonist status to negotiation agenda and political cost of the opposition, with diplomatic track reopened (Greer × Mauro Vieira) and reading of "bill on the table of Bolsonarism".
